newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - SEPT 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - SEPT 13.

text.p: PRAVO - The minimum wage has nothing to do with the poverty level according to the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs. The minimum wage is currently 2500 crowns a month while the poverty level is 2660 crowns a month and will be increased to 2890 a month in October.

- The recent decision by the Polish government to restrict the construction of foreign automobiles does not affect the Skoda automobile manufacturer according to press spokesperson Milan Smutny. Skoda will observe the Polish government's conditions he stated.

- Ceska Sporitelna intends to lay off several thousand workers and significantly decrease the number of branches operating in the Czech Republic. In the next five years the number of employees should decrease from the current 19 thousand to between 12 and 14 thousand.

- Costs for the modernization of the railway corridor from Decin-Prague-Breclav will increase to at least 32 billion crowns instead of the 24 billion crowns originally approved by the government in the 1994 budget.
- Eurotel will offer the transmission of short messages with the use of a small keyboard on their mobile phones, according to the company's press spokeswoman, Iva Tatounova.

- The Brno-based Escom CS, a daughter company of the German manufacturer and distributor of computers Escom AG, has become copmpletely independant from its mother company. Both companies have long been connected only through capital and by name for quite a while, accordin to the vice-chairman of Escom CS's board of directors.

- In the last two years, the DuPont chemical company has increased its sales by 30 percent in the Czech Republic. This indicator should exceed 100 billion dollars. HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - A two-day meeting of leaders of CEFTA member states and their Central and Eastern European counterparts will begin today in Jasna in Slovakia's Low Tatra mountains.

- CZ-Cagiva a.s., a Czech-Italian motorcycle manufacturer, intends to decrease its basic capital from 961 million crowns to approximately 160 million crowns during an upcoming shareholders meeting according to the general manager of CZ Strakonice, Jan Kunes. CZ Strakonice still owns a 10.4 percent share in the motorcycle manufacturer.
- Skoda Plzen and Trinecke Zelezarny signed an agreement on cooperation and coordination in metallurgical production according to Skoda's press spokesperson, Karel Samec.
